title: Weil extension of rational maps to an abelian variety
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a nonempty integral separated $k$-scheme of finite type [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $B/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme, and let $f:U\to B$ be a $k$-scheme morphism. There exists a unique $k$-scheme morphism $\overline f:X\to B$ whose restriction to $U$ is $f$.

source.place: 8.18, printed p.152 (combine 8.16 and 8.17). Uniqueness is the separated-target equality principle on an integral source. This is the extension theorem, not extension to an arbitrary proper target.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal], with the identity field extension $k/k$, $X$ is regular and all its local rings are normal domains. By [def-weil-regular-scheme], it is locally Noetherian and its local rings are Noetherian. Its structure map is quasi-compact by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], so $X$ is Noetherian. By [def-pc-integral-scheme] $X$ is reduced and irreducible. By [def-sc-abelian-variety], $B$ is a proper smooth connected group scheme, hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. It therefore has all the target hypotheses for both the proper-target extension input and the group-target input.

source.place: 8.18, printed p.152, combining 8.16 and 8.17; expanded using Milne Abelian Varieties, Chapter I, Theorems 3.1–3.2 and Lemma 3.3, printed pp.16–18.

proof.text: Consider all pairs $(V,F_V)$ with $V$ open in $X$, $U\subseteq V$, and $F_V:V\to B$ a $k$-morphism extending $f$. Let $D$ be the union of their domains. The pair $(U,f)$ belongs to this family. For any two pairs, $U$ is dense in $V\cap V'$: an open subset of this intersection is open in $X$ and meets the dense $U$. The intersection is reduced, since all its stalks are stalks of the reduced $X$ [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The maps agree on $U$ and are over $k$, so [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] gives equality on $V\cap V'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to obtain $F_D:D\to B$. Its composite to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ agrees with the structure map on every $V$, so the uniqueness clause of gluing makes $F_D$ a $k$-morphism. Also $F_D|_U=f$.

source.place: Tag 0A1Y, lemma-rational-map-from-reduced-to-separated, proof by gluing representatives; the relative equality and gluing assertions are the cited nodes.

proof.text: Let $x\in X$ satisfy $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=1$. Step 1 makes $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ a Noetherian normal local domain, so [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] makes it a discrete valuation ring. By [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] it is a valuation ring. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-map-extension-valuation-point] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $Y=B$, and the original $U,f$. The source is integral and Noetherian by step 1, the target is proper, and $U$ is dense. The cited statement gives an open $V$ containing $U$ and $x$ and a $k$-morphism extending $f$. This is one of the pairs defining $D$, hence $x\in D$. Thus $X\setminus D$ contains no point with one-dimensional local ring.

source.place: Chapter I, Theorem 3.1, printed pp.16–17, the codimension-one DVR argument; Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr) and morphisms.tex Tag 0BX7 (lemma-extend-across), in the cited existing nodes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-group-rational-divisorial-indeterminacy] to the given smooth integral $X$, to $G=B$, and to $U,f$. Its $D$ is exactly the union in step 2; smoothness, connectedness, separatedness and finite type of $B$ were verified in step 1. If $D\ne X$, the cited statement supplies a nonempty finite collection of closed subsets $Z_i\subseteq X\setminus D$ and generic points $z_i$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,z_i}=1$. In particular $z_1\notin D$, contradicting step 3. Therefore $D=X$. The morphism $F_D$ of step 2 is the required extension.

source.place: 8.18, printed p.152, combining 8.16 and 8.17; expanded using Milne Abelian Varieties, Chapter I, Theorems 3.1–3.2 and Lemma 3.3, printed pp.16–18.

proof.text: If $F,F':X\to B$ are two $k$-morphisms restricting to $f$ on $U$, apply [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] with $T=X$, $W=U$, $Y=B$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $h$ the open inclusion. The source is reduced, $h$ has dense image, the target is separated over $k$, and $Fh=f=F'h$. Hence $F=F'$.

I Thm 3.1, Thm 3.2 and Lemma 3.3 (printed pp.16–18; k arbitrary, varieties geometrically reduced). The route is 8.16 in pointwise form plus 8.17, giving 8.18. Step 1: lem-trf-smooth-geometrically-normal with K'=K=k gives regular, normal-domain local rings; with finite type this makes X Noetherian. B is proper, so it is separated and of finite type. Step 2: V∩V' is reduced and U is dense in it, so relative-separated-dominant-ext applies; gluing gives F_D on the maximal domain D, and the uniqueness clause shows F_D is over k. Step 3: a 1-dimensional Noetherian normal local domain is a DVR, hence a valuation ring; rational-map-extension-valuation-point (all hypotheses checked) puts every codimension-1 point in D. Step 4: the new node forces D=X. Step 5: uniqueness follows from the dense-equality lemma. New node lem-sfb-group-rational-divisorial-indeterminacy is Milne 8.17 / AV 3.3 for arbitrary k with smooth X and a smooth separated group G. It is true. Small cases checked: dim 0, U=X, a constant map, G_a with f=1/t (complement is a divisor, so properness of G is genuinely not assumed) and the trivial group. It does not restate the parent and is not a duplicate: a DAG statement scan and the Mathlib RationalMap API found no Weil purity result.
